questions.question: Solve x² + 8x + 3 = 0 by completing the square, showing every step, and explain how the same working produces the turning point of y = x² + 8x + 3.
questions.expected_answer: Move the constant across: x² + 8x = −3. The completing number is the square of half the coefficient of x: half of 8 is 4 and 4² = 16, added to both sides to keep the equation balanced, giving x² + 8x + 16 = 13. The left side is a perfect square, so (x + 4)² = 13. Square-rooting both sides introduces a plus-or-minus, since both √13 and −√13 square to 13: x + 4 = ±√13, so x = −4 + √13 or x = −4 − √13. For the graph, add and subtract 16 inside the expression: x² + 8x + 3 = (x + 4)² − 16 + 3 = (x + 4)² − 13, which is the form (x + p)² + q, so the turning point is (−4; −13) and the axis of symmetry is x = −4.

questions.question: Derive the quadratic formula from ax² + bx + c = 0 by completing the square, and name the two structural features of the result that cost learners the most marks.
questions.expected_answer: Divide every term by a (allowed since a ≠ 0): x² + (b/a)x + c/a = 0. Move the constant: x² + (b/a)x = −c/a. Half of b/a is b/(2a); its square is b²/(4a²); add that to both sides. The left side becomes (x + b/2a)² and the right side becomes b²/(4a²) − c/a = (b² − 4ac)/(4a²) over the common denominator. Square-rooting both sides gives x + b/(2a) = ±√(b² − 4ac)/(2a), since √(4a²) = 2a. Subtracting b/(2a) and combining gives x = [−b ± √(b² − 4ac)]/(2a). The two mark-costing features: first, the 2a divides the entire numerator, the −b included, not only the root; second, the sign of b — when b is negative, −b becomes positive and b² is positive, so both must be handled with brackets at substitution.

questions.question: For 2x² − 9x + 3 = 0, give the exact solutions and the solutions correct to two decimal places, and explain how to decide between factorising, completing the square and the formula.
questions.expected_answer: With a = 2, b = −9 and c = 3, the discriminant is (−9)² − 4(2)(3) = 81 − 24 = 57, so x = (9 ± √57)/4, the exact answer required when simplest surd form is asked. Since √57 ≈ 7,5498, the roots are (9 + 7,5498)/4 ≈ 4,14 and (9 − 7,5498)/4 ≈ 0,36, correct to two decimal places; rounding may only happen at this final line, because rounding √57 to 7,5 earlier shifts the second decimal to 4,13 and 0,38. Method choice: factorise whenever the discriminant is a perfect square, since it is fastest and exact; use the formula when the discriminant is not a perfect square, since it never fails; complete the square when the question names the method or asks for the turning point, since only that method produces the form a(x + p)² + q directly.
